nodes.summary: Let $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ be a potential. If there is a radial scattering solution $w$ to the scattering equation with potential $v$, the scattering length of $v$ is $a(v) = (8\pi)^{-1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} v(x)\,(1 - w(x))\,dx$, where $w$ is one such solution, chosen arbitrarily; if there is no radial scattering solution, $a(v) = 0$.
nodes.title: Scattering length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a real number $L$, the box $([0,L]^3)^N$ is the set of configurations $(x_1, \dots, x_N)$ of $N$ points of $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every coordinate of every point $x_i$ lies in the closed interval $[0, L]$.
nodes.title: The box $((0,L)^3)^N$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a real number $L$, $C_0^\infty(([0,L]^3)^N) \setminus \{0\}$ consists of the functions $\Psi : (\mathbb{R}^3)^N \to \mathbb{R}$ that are smooth on the box $([0,L]^3)^N$, whose closed support is contained in the interior of the box, and that are not identically zero.
nodes.title: Smooth functions supported inside the box

nodes.summary: A function $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ is radial if $v(x) = v(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\|x\| = \|y\|$.
nodes.title: Radial functions

nodes.summary: Let $v, w : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$. The function $w$ is a scattering solution for the potential $v$ if $w$ and $v\,(1 - w)$ are locally integrable, $w(x) \to 0$ as $\|x\| \to \infty$, and $w$ solves the scattering equation $-\Delta w = \frac{1}{2} v\,(1 - w)$ (Equation (3.4) of Fournais–Solovej) in the weak sense: for every smooth, compactly supported $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$,
nodes.title: Scattering solutions

nodes.summary: $\eta$ is a real constant, not given explicitly, that serves as the exponent in the error term $(\rho a^3)^{1/2 + \eta}$ of the Lee–Huang–Yang lower bound (Theorem 1.2), where $\rho$ is the density and $a$ the scattering length of the potential; that theorem asserts $\eta > 0$.

nodes.title: Lee–Huang–Yang error constant

nodes.summary: For a potential $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ with scattering length $a(v)$, let $\mathcal{R}(v) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} v(x)/(8\pi a(v))\,dx$. When $a(v) \neq 0$ this is the ratio of $(8\pi)^{-1} \int v$ to $a(v)$.
nodes.title: The ratio $\mathcal{R}(v)$
